expectedMisconceptions: Sorting samples by colour alone is the most common shortcut children take — exactly the trap Atlas warns against in the mission's own story beat, so it's worth checking each group uses more than one observed property.

A classification can feel 'wrong' to a child if it doesn't match what they expect a sample to be — remind them a classification only needs to be justified by evidence, not by a guess at the sample's true identity.
stretchQuestions: Could a single sample reasonably belong to more than one of your groups? What would you do about that?
What additional property, if you could observe it, would make your classification even more reliable?
estimatedSupervision: Minimal — works well as an independent investigation; a parent may enjoy hearing the justification for each group afterwards.
